description: A Java routine's RETURNS clause may carry TYPE PARAMETERS - VARCHAR(100), DECIMAL(10,2), NUMBER(5), TIMESTAMP(9), TIMESTAMP_NTZ(6), and for procedures VARCHAR(50) and DECIMAL(15,4) - and a routine whose handler's Java type carries the declared type creates and answers. The parameters are part of the signature's shape but not of its identity: two overloads may declare different return widths, and CREATE OR REPLACE may widen the return type of an existing routine, after which the new handler's longer value comes back whole. Declaring no parameters at all keeps working, which is the backward-compatible case. Converted 1:1 from udf/ReturnTypeParametersTest (now retired), a JDBC test whose statements are all plain SQL. A handler whose Java type cannot carry the declared SQL type is refused when the routine is created, naming Snowflake's storage type: a double handler for a DECIMAL, a String one for a TIMESTAMP.
